preparation_status: v1 and v2 not adopted; preserve invalid old caches and infeasible old-workspace solves
scope: Historical matrix-graph fractional LP objective divided into matched-chip matched-width streaming cost; fixed mapping template and fixed hardware resource budgets; width-only timing sensitivity, not native precision validation.
method: Use archived tile-qualified c0 mapping only; exclude alternative PE/sys/VPU hardware geometries.
Preserve graph, source operation count, tensor associations, first imports and original LP approximations.
INT8/BF16 headings denote 8/16-bit stored-operand width; scale bytes, workspace and memory terms by width; retain the same compute/accumulator timing proxy and do not give INT8 a throughput bonus.
Reprice c0 compute to each hardware MAC budget and memory to each hardware bandwidth.
Reference is sum of repriced per-operation c0 T_max at the same width and hardware; no host-policy substitution.
Objective is V2.1 serial-reload LP with byte-consistent traffic floors and fixed SRAM; UNet uses the DAG producer.
Ratios below one reflect that the LP serial-reload/tensor-floor cost exceeds the independently modeled streaming reference, not a measured slowdown.
limitations: Not an actual quantization or BF16 numerical-equivalence test.
No new Timeloop runs: archived tile coefficients are repriced analytically.
Compact-NPU mapping costs are analytical resource scaling of the fixed source template, not a fresh native compact-NPU mapping.
No recovered integer execution, native TPU-v3 INT8 capability claim, exact rational certificate or full autoregressive decode result.
Inherited S0=0 workspace approximation; single-predecessor graphs except UNet; no change to current co-design results or figures.
